Definition: middle voice from G303 and G2192; to hold oneself up against, i.e. (figuratively) put up with:--bear with, endure, forbear, suffer.
BiblicalUsage: To bear with, to put up with, to hold oneself up against the weight of another person's faults. Paul tells the churches to forbear one another in love and to forgive as Christ forgave, Jesus asks how long He shall suffer a faithless generation, and Hebrews asks its readers to suffer the word of exhortation.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe bearing with one another is the daily proof of love, harder than any single act of forgiveness and longer than any single argument. Christ bore with me first, and I hold that His patience with me is the measure of the patience I owe His people.
